outputs.L1: A daylighting film (1) according to an aspect of the invention includes a first base (2), a plurality of daylighting portions (3) formed by polygonal prism structures, and gaps (9) provided between the daylighting portions (3). In a cross section orthogonal to its longitudinal direction, each daylighting portion (3) has a polygonal shape with four vertices, all interior angles of which are less than 180°. The polygon has a first side corresponding to a surface in contact with the first base (2) and a plurality of vertices, including first and second vertices corresponding to respective ends of the first side and a third vertex not located on the first side. The length of a line perpendicular to the first side and passing through the third vertex is greater than the lengths of lines perpendicular to the first side and passing through the vertices other than the third vertex. The daylighting portion (3) is asymmetrical about the line perpendicular to the first side and passing through the third vertex.
outputs.L2: In one aspect of the invention, a daylighting film (1) comprises a first base (2), multiple daylighting portions (3) formed from polygonal prism structures, and gaps (9) separating the daylighting portions (3). In a cross-section perpendicular to its longitudinal direction, each daylighting portion (3) has a four-vertex polygonal profile in which every interior angle is smaller than 180°. The polygon includes a first side corresponding to the surface contacting the first base (2), first and second vertices located at opposite ends of the first side, and a third vertex situated away from the first side. The perpendicular distance from the first side to the third vertex exceeds the corresponding perpendicular distances from the first side to each of the other vertices. Furthermore, the daylighting portion (3) is not symmetric about the line that passes through the third vertex and is perpendicular to the first side.
outputs.L3:
The daylighting film includes a first base and a plurality of daylighting portions disposed on the first base, with gaps provided between adjacent daylighting portions. Each daylighting portion is formed as a polygonal prism extending in a longitudinal direction and has a four-vertex polygonal cross-section in a plane perpendicular to that longitudinal direction.

The polygonal cross-section is convex, such that each of its interior angles is less than 180 degrees. A first side of the polygonal cross-section is in contact with the first base. First and second vertices are located at opposite ends of the first side, while a third vertex is positioned apart from the first side. Among the vertices of the cross-section, the third vertex has the greatest perpendicular distance from the first side. In addition, the daylighting portion has an asymmetrical shape with respect to a line that passes through the third vertex and is perpendicular to the first side.
outputs.L4:
A daylighting film includes a light-transmitting base and a plurality of polygonal prism-shaped daylighting portions arranged on one surface of the base. Adjacent daylighting portions are spaced apart by gaps rather than being formed continuously. In a cross-section taken perpendicular to the longitudinal direction of each prism, each daylighting portion has a polygonal profile defined by four vertices. The vertices are connected in sequence so that every interior angle of the profile is less than 180 degrees, thereby forming a convex cross-sectional shape.

Among the four vertices, the third vertex is positioned farther from the base than each of the other vertices and thus forms the unique highest point of the daylighting portion. A line extending from the third vertex perpendicular to the base defines a reference axis for the prism profile. The portions of the cross-section located on opposite sides of this axis differ from one another, such that the profile is not mirror-symmetric about the perpendicular line. This asymmetrical configuration allows incident daylight to be refracted, reflected, or redirected preferentially toward a selected direction. Accordingly, the film can introduce natural light into an interior space while providing greater control over the direction and distribution of the transmitted light.
outputs.L5:
## Each

“Each” is used to refer to every individual person or thing in a group separately. It emphasizes the members one by one rather than the group as a whole.

For example:

- Each student received a book.
- The tickets cost ten dollars each.
- Each of the rooms has a window.

“Each” is generally followed by a singular noun and a singular verb: “Each child is welcome.” It can also appear after a plural subject, as in “The children each received a gift.”

Unlike “every,” which considers all members collectively, “each” places greater emphasis on individuality. For example, “Each employee has a responsibility” highlights the responsibility of every employee separately.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract describing a daylighting film with a base, separated polygonal prism daylighting portions, and asymmetric quadrilateral cross-sections.
counterfactuals.output: A daylighting film includes a base having a first surface and a second surface opposite the first surface, and a plurality of discrete daylighting portions arranged on the first surface. The daylighting portions are spaced apart from one another and extend as polygonal prisms along respective longitudinal directions. Each daylighting portion has a cross-section, transverse to its longitudinal direction, defining an asymmetric quadrilateral having first and second inclined light-refracting faces of different lengths, slopes, or angular orientations. The asymmetric quadrilateral cross-sections are configured to receive incident daylight through one of the base and the daylighting portions and redirect the daylight toward a selected interior region. Separation between adjacent daylighting portions provides intervening substantially planar regions of the base and facilitates controlled transmission, refraction, and distribution of daylight.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a detailed technical description of a daylighting film invention, preserving reference numerals (1), (2), (3), and (9) and defining the geometry of each prism structure.
counterfactuals.output:
A daylighting film **(1)** is formed as an optically transparent sheet having a substantially planar light-exit surface and an opposite structured light-incident surface. The structured surface includes a repeated array of a first prism structure **(2)**, a second prism structure **(3)**, and, optionally or periodically, a third prism structure **(9)**. The prism structures extend longitudinally in a common extrusion direction and redirect obliquely incident daylight by refraction, total internal reflection, or a combination thereof.

A Cartesian coordinate system may be defined such that the film plane lies in the \(x\)-\(y\) plane, the thickness direction is the \(z\)-direction, and the longitudinal axes of the prism structures are parallel to the \(y\)-axis. The geometry of each prism structure is therefore defined principally by its cross-section in the \(x\)-\(z\) plane.

The first prism structure **(2)** has a triangular cross-section bounded by a first planar facet and a second planar facet that meet at an apex. The first facet forms an inclination angle \(\alpha_2\) with the nominal plane of the film, while the second facet forms an inclination angle \(\beta_2\) with that plane. The apex angle is consequently

\[
\gamma_2 = 180^\circ-\alpha_2-\beta_2.
\]

The first prism structure **(2)** has a base width \(w_2\), a height \(h_2\), and a longitudinally extending apex ridge. Its apex may be centered over the base when \(\alpha_2=\beta_2\), or laterally offset when the two facet angles differ. An asymmetric configuration is particularly suitable for redirecting daylight arriving at a predetermined elevation angle.

The second prism structure **(3)** is positioned adjacent to the first prism structure **(2)** and likewise extends in the longitudinal direction. In cross-section, the second prism structure **(3)** may be triangular or truncated triangular. In the triangular configuration, it includes first and second facets inclined by respective angles \(\alpha_3\) and \(\beta_3\), giving an apex angle

\[
\gamma_3 = 180^\circ-\alpha_3-\beta_3.
\]

It has a base width \(w_3\) and a height \(h_3\). In the truncated configuration, the two inclined facets are connected by a substantially planar crest having a width \(c_3\), so that the structure has a trapezoidal cross-section. At least one of \(\alpha_3\), \(\beta_3\), \(w_3\), and \(h_3\) differs from the corresponding parameter of the first prism structure **(2)**. The second prism structure **(3)** therefore redirects a different portion of the incident angular distribution, broadening the useful range of solar elevation angles.

The third prism structure **(9)** is disposed between selected first and second prism structures or is repeated at a lower spatial frequency than the structures **(2)** and **(3)**. The third prism structure **(9)** has a polygonal cross-section comprising an entrance facet, a principal redirecting facet, and, where required, an intermediate or relief facet. The entrance facet is inclined by an angle \(\alpha_9\), and the principal redirecting facet is inclined by an angle \(\beta_9\), relative to the nominal film plane. If the facets meet directly, the apex angle is

\[
\gamma_9 = 180^\circ-\alpha_9-\beta_9.
\]

If an intermediate facet is present, the structure **(9)** has a broken or compound profile characterized by a lower facet angle \(\alpha_{9a}\), an upper facet angle \(\alpha_{9b}\), a base width \(w_9\), and a total height \(h_9\). This compound geometry can suppress unwanted downward redirection, reduce optical coupling between adjacent prisms, or provide an additional redirection band for low- or high-elevation daylight.

The structures **(2)**, **(3)**, and **(9)** may be arranged in a repeating unit having pitch

\[
P=w_2+w_3+w_9+s,
\]

where \(s\) represents any intervening planar land or manufacturing clearance. Preferably, neighboring structures meet without a substantial land so that the structured surface has a high optical fill factor. The apex ridges may be sharp, or they may have a radius of curvature selected to permit replication while remaining small relative to the relevant prism width.

The film **(1)** is manufactured from a transparent polymer whose refractive index is greater than that of the surrounding air, enabling the inclined facets to redirect incident light according to Snell’s law and, at appropriate incidence angles, by total internal reflection. The differing geometries of the prism structures **(2)**, **(3)**, and **(9)** provide multiple angular response ranges within a single film **(1)**, thereby redirecting daylight toward an interior ceiling or deeper into a building while limiting glare and direct downward transmission.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an optical daylighting sheet whose projecting portions have convex four-vertex cross-sections, with one vertex farther from the base than the others and an asymmetric profile about that vertex.
counterfactuals.output: An optical daylighting sheet comprises a transparent base layer and multiple elongated projecting portions formed on at least one surface of the base. In a cross-section perpendicular to each projection’s longitudinal direction, each projecting portion has a convex quadrilateral profile. One vertex forms an apex located farther from the base surface than the other three vertices. The two sides extending from this apex differ in inclination, length, or shape, so the cross-section is not mirror-symmetric about a line passing through the apex and normal to the base. This asymmetric geometry refracts and/or reflects incident daylight preferentially in a selected direction, such as deeper into a room or toward a ceiling.
